This petition is filed by the petitioners/accused
Nos.2 and 3 under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. for quashing the criminal proceedings in
C.C.No.3733/2024 pending on the file of IV-Addl. Civil Judge & Jmfc, Kalaburagi, arising out of
Crime No.137/2023 registered by the M.B.Nagar police and charge-sheeted for the offence
punishable under Sections 323, 498-A, 504, 506 read with Section 34 Ipc.
2. Heard the arguments of the learned counsel for the petitioners and learned High Court Government NC: 2024:KHC-K:6742 Pleader for respondent No.1/State.
Respondent served and unrepresented.
3. The case of the petitioners is that on the complaint filed by the respondent No.2, the police registered the FIR on 16.11.2023.
It is alleged by her that she was married to the son of these petitioners on 12.05.2015.
After the marriage she was stayed in Kalaburagi for three months.
Later the accused No.1 took her to Bangalore and she stayed at Bangalore for seven months.
Thereafter, he brought her and left her in the parents house i.e. house of the present petitioners' i.e. accused Nos.2 and 3.
There is a son born to the respondent No.2.

He is studying in 2nd standard, but the accused No.1 said to be not properly coming to the Kalaburagi and abusing and harassing her in filthy Gurupadappa And Anr vs The State Of Karnataka And Anr on 9 September, 2024

Due to the non toleration she said to be consumed the pesticide.
She was admitted in the Hospital, MLC sent to the police.

Accordingly, the police obtained the complaint,
registered the FIR against NC: 2024:KHC-K:6742 accused No.1.
After the investigation, they filed the charge-sheet by including these petitioners, which is under challenge.

4. The learned counsel for the petitioners submits that there is no allegation against these petitioners in the complaint and their names are not mentioned in the FIR, but after two months the further statement recorded by the police implicated these petitioners.
There is no demand of dowry or harassment, ill-treatment by these petitioners, except the allegation that they are not eating the food cooked by the respondent No.2.
Therefore, it is contended that the continuation of proceedings against these petitioners is nothing but abuse of process law.
The petitioner/accused No.2 is a retired Government Teacher and his wife was also senior citizen and the police have falsely implicated them.
Hence, prayed for quashing the criminal proceedings.
The learned High Court Government Pleader has seriously objected the petition and prayed for dismissal of petition.
6. Having heard arguments of learned counsel for both parties and on perusal of records, which reveals that the marriage of the accused No.1 with respondent No.2 was on 12.05.2015.
The complaint came to be filed in 2023, after seven years of the marriage.

It is seen from the records that accused No.1 after the marriage took the complainant to the Bangalore and stayed in Bangalore for seven months, but later she was brought back and left in the house of these petitioners/accused Nos.2 and 3 and she was residing with the accused Nos.2 and 3 i.e. the present petitioners.
In the complaint she has not stated the names of these petitioners, whether they are harassed her physically and mentally in order to attract Section 498-A of IPC.

It is also seen from the complaint that the accused No.1 harassing her through phone and though often and often he used to visit where he used to quarrel NC: 2024:KHC-K:6742 and abused her in filthy language, but she has not stated anything about these petitioners and only implicated in the charge sheet by recording the further statement stating that they said to be not ate the food cooked by her, except that there is no other allegations against these petitioners.
They are aged about 69 and 65 years and the respondent No.2 was residing with them for almost six years, there is no ill-treatment or complaint by her against these petitioners, except accused No.1.
Therefore, continuing of criminal proceedings against these petitioners is nothing but abuse of process of law.

Hence, I pass the following:
ORDER i) The petition is allowed.
